transcript:
Meeting header
Date/time: 2025-01-28 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood SE), Rachel (SummitPay Eng Mgr), Dev (SummitPay Sr Backend), Laura (SummitPay Security), Tom (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): walk through SDK quickstarts for Python and TypeScript, auth choices (api key, sso), env setup incl. k8s/CI notes, plan pilot; asked for security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick SDK integration walkthrough, focus on Python and TypeScript quickstarts, and then i'll hand to diego for streaming/caching bits.
[00:12] Rachel: thanks, stoked
we've got a 6 week timeline for a pilot, want to validate latency and cost before committing to dedicated capacity.
[00:20] Samira: perfect, that aligns. quick q: are you planning to use hosted api or private deployment?
[00:28] Dev: initially hosted, but compliance might push us to dedicated or VPC, so we want both options considered.
[00:36] Diego: good note. for the SDKs we support both flows the same way; auth is the main diff
api key for hosted, and SAML/SSO + mTLS/KMS for private.
[00:48] Maya: i'll share the SSO doc later
small heads up, the term "Redwood Private" sometimes shows up as "Redwood Privatee" in some docs, ignore the extra e, it's just OCR from older exports.
[00:58] Tom: (laugh) noted. ok can you show the python quickstart?
[01:05] Samira: yes. so python pip install redwood-inference-sdk, set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var, then example: from redwood import Client; client = Client(); resp = client.generate("summitpay transaction summary prompt")
streaming example is slightly different, diego?
[01:28] Diego: right, for streaming in python you do client.stream(...), we yield tokens. i'll paste sample snippet after. note that for streaming to keep latency low set chunk_size to 128 and use our continuous batching option
it's auto but you can tune.
[01:45] Rachel: about auth in CI
we prefer short-lived creds; can we rotate api keys automatically?
[01:52] Maya: yes, you can use our temporary token exchange API and integrate with your secrets manager. for private deployments you can federate via your idp SAML/OIDC and we integrate with SSO, RBAC, and SCIM provisioning.
[02:10] Laura: can you confirm encryption at rest and KMS options? we need customer-managed keys.
[02:16] Diego: yes, customer-managed KMS supported in Private; hosted also supports envelope encryption with our KMS but we can do a contract for CMK in Dedicated. i'll put the KMS diagram in the follow-up.
[02:30] Dev: for the typescript example, what package?
[02:34] Samira: npm install @redwood-inference/sdk
then import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk'; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const resp = await client.chat.create({model: 'rwd-4b', input: 'summarize...'}); note model names vary, and 'rwd-4b' in docs is example only. sometimes transcription shows model names like "road-4b" or "rw-4b"
ignore those typos.
[03:05] Rachel: are there TypeScript typings?
[03:07] Maya: yes full typings and examples for node + browser. for browser you should proxy requests to keep api key off client, or use ephemeral tokens.
[03:18] Tom: ok how about environment setup? we use k8s, GitHub Actions, and Hashi vault. quickstart for CI?
[03:25] Diego: recommended pattern
store REDWOOD_API_KEY in vault, use ephemeral token step: we provide an action that exchanges service account creds for short-lived token, then pass token into job. i'll send the GH action example.
[03:40] Dev: latency/cost
what's the rough tokens/sec and cost per token?
[03:45] Samira: costs depend on model & quantization; rwd-4b ~0.6ms per token on our dedicated infra with batching, hosted a bit higher. we'll share the perf matrix. for cost we have per-token pricing on hosted, and reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated. Diego: also, caching and prefix caching can reduce tokens; Optimize suggests quantization and batch sizes per workload.
[04:15] Rachel: procurement will ask for SOC2 and net diagram. Laura: also need data retention policy.
[04:22] Maya: we have a SOC2 kit and security whitepaper, plus network diagrams
i'll attach links in the email.
[04:30] Laura: any caveats about PII? we want to keep PII out of training and logs.
[04:35] Diego: by default hosted stores logs for 30 days for debugging but you can disable logging and set zero retention on private/dedicated. we also support audit logs and redaction hooks.
[04:50] Samira: demo time: i'll quickly step through a live python run (note: minor audio interruptions)
[04:56] [screen share noise] Samira: okay running pip install
installing... and then export REDWOOD_API_KEY to env, run example. you'll see the streaming tokens come in.
[05:20] Rachel: i see output - looks good. question: what about error handling & fallbacks?
[05:25] Diego: sdk has built-in retries, and you can configure fallback model variants; routing policies let you prefer lower-cost model first then fallback to premium if latency allows.
[05:40] Tom: for pilot we want a small set of prompts and an eval harness. do you have a quick eval flow?
[05:46] Maya: yes Optimize includes eval sets; simplest is send 100 prompts to two model variants and compare latency/cost + human quality score. we can supply the eval script.
[06:00] Dev: about network egress
if we use hosted in us-west, can we guarantee routes don't leave region?
[06:06] Diego: we can pin regions for hosted; for strict requirements, Dedicated or Private with VPC is best.
[06:12] Rachel: timeline: we want pilot by next week
is that feasible?
[06:16] Samira: yes, we can provision sandbox keys and a small hosted quota immediately; dedicated sizing takes longer.
[06:22] [timestamp jumps, paraphrase]
[06:40] Samira: i'll summarize artifacts i'll send: pricing tier summary, python + ts snippets, GH action example, SOC2 + network diagrams, Dedicated sizing questionnaire.
[06:52] Rachel: great. Logistics: who will be main contact?
[06:55] Rachel: i'll be PM, Dev will do infra, Laura will handle security questions.
[07:02] Samira: noted. action items on me and diego.
[07:06] Maya: quick note
endpoints: api.redwood.ai/v1 for hosted, private has customer-specific endpoint like ingress.mycompany.redwood.internal
examples in quickstart.
[07:18] Dev: got it. any rate limits to be aware of?
[07:22] Diego: hosted has soft rate limits; Dedicated you can configure throughput targets. for pilot we'll set a low quota to begin.
[07:35] Tom: can you show the TS streaming snippet real quick?
[07:38] Samira: sure, const stream = client.chat.stream({model:'rwd-4b', input: '...'}); for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk.delta); } same idea as python but async iteration.
[07:58] Rachel: ok last sec security q: does Redwood provide an attestation or SOC2 artifact exchange process?
[08:05] Maya: yes we use secure file transfer for artifacts and have an NDA/POA process if needed.
[08:12] [wrap-up]
[08:15] Samira: recap and next steps: we'll share sandbox key + quickstarts, diego will send sample scripts, maya will attach security docs, rachel to share stakeholder list. schedule pilot kickoff for next tuesday?
[08:30] Rachel: tuesday works for us. thanks everyone.

Notes on transcription quality: a few words misheard (model names, minor typos), occasional speaker misattribution where system labeled multiple Redwoods as 'Speaker 1'.
